subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core own Anthropic pace-aware agent throttling, or should core stop at provider usage/status/context primitives for plugins and future policy layers?
rationale: The remaining work adds provider-specific pacing semantics, new config, persistence, and autonomous runtime behavior that can change agent execution, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Visibility-first core contract
options.body: Add provider pace/status/session-context primitives in core while deferring automatic throttling policy until the semantics are proven.

options.title: Full core throttling policy
options.body: Accept a larger core feature with config, persisted pace state, notifications, and opt-in throttling semantics for autonomous agents.

options.title: Plugin-owned pacing
options.body: Keep core limited to existing usage APIs and route pace-tier policy to a provider plugin or ClawHub extension if SDK seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Visibility-first core contract
recommendation.body: Add provider pace/status/session-context primitives in core while deferring automatic throttling policy until the semantics are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal for the provider usage hooks and shared Claude usage-window builder that would anchor the product decision.
